planting.note: Plant dormant canes or containerized transplants in late winter through early spring, spacing to allow good airflow; this historic English floricane type benefits from a wire trellis to support its vigorous canes.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Malling Landmark is a historic English floricane raspberry raised in the breeding program at East Malling Research Station in Kent, part of the mid-20th-century maternal lineage that also produced Malling Promise and, through later crosses undertaken in Scotland, contributed to the parentage of modern Glen-series raspberries including Glen Moy. It bears medium-sized, firm, well-flavored red fruit on vigorous canes in summer. Prune out spent floricanes after harvest and thin new canes to the strongest few per foot of row.
sources: East Malling Research Station historical variety records

common_name: Magic of Oz Daylily (Light Pink Spider with Emerald Green Throat)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this Herrington spider-form introduction, registered in 1995, rewards generous spacing with tall, well-branched scapes.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Magic of Oz is a spider-form daylily bearing large, light pink flowers about seven inches across with an emerald-green throat, held on tall, well-branched 37-inch scapes. Registered by H. Herrington in 1995, it blooms midseason and later earned the AHS Award of Merit (2003) and Harris Olson Spider Award (2005), and was used as a parent of Journey to Oz. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.
